title: ARTEX Explained: An AI Team That Pentests on Its Own
description: What ARTEX is, what makes it different from a scanner or a single chatbot, and how its team of AI agents plans, works, remembers and finishes a security test with little human help.
audience: Anyone curious how an autonomous multi-agent AI system works, no code reading needed.

chapters.title: Highlights
chapters.summary: Eight cards on an AI team that pentests on its own: the roles, the shared memory, the guard rails, and the decisions a planner faces.

chapters.title: How ARTEX Fits Together
chapters.summary: Tour the agent team, the work it produces, its shared memory and its guard rails, then rebuild the map from memory.

chapters.title: You Are the Planner
chapters.summary: Step into the team lead's shoes: ten wake-ups, ten decisions about what the agent team should do next.

chapters.title: The Stalled Task
chapters.summary: A lab task stopped making progress overnight. Use the team's own records to work out which part of the agent loop was waiting, and why.

chapters.title: ARTEX Archipelago
chapters.summary: One island per big idea, hands-on activities, then a final exam over the whole system.

objectives: Describe the parts of ARTEX: the goals agent, planner, workers, shared graphs and guard rails, and how they fit together
Explain what makes an agent team different from a scanner or a single chatbot with tools
Decide what the team lead should do next at each wake-up, given the team's state
Trace a stalled task through the team's own records to the part of the loop that was waiting
prerequisites: A rough idea of what a penetration test is

glossary.definition: A program that uses a language model to decide its next action, acts with tools, reads the result and goes again.
The agent that turns goals into work orders for the workers and keeps the to-do list.
One concrete intent handed to a worker: what to try, against what, and what counts as done.
Something a worker observed and recorded, with evidence, in the shared memory.
A confirmed security weakness, built from facts, that goes into the report.
The team's shared memory of what has been found and tried, so no agent repeats work or forgets a lead.
A point where a risky action waits for the human operator to say yes.
The systems the test is allowed to touch; anything else is off limits however interesting.
